claims.claim: PROGRESS.md pre-clear checkpoint is Tier 1 standard for session continuity
claims.citation: Before reaching context limit, ask Claude to summarize: accomplishments, files modified with rationale, next 3 steps, decisions/constraints - save to PROGRESS.md. Then run /clear and paste summary back into fresh session.

claims.claim: /handover command generates structured HANDOVER.md with decisions, pitfalls, lessons, failed approaches
claims.citation: Custom slash command /handover generates a HANDOVER.md at session end capturing: decisions, pitfalls, lessons, failed approaches (do not repeat), key decisions with rationale, current state (working vs broken), resume instructions with numbered steps.

claims.claim: /handover pattern is widely copied with independent implementations (claude-handoff, mcpmarket tools)
claims.citation: Plugin repos at https://github.com/willseltzer/claude-handoff and https://mcpmarket.com/tools/skills/session-handover confirm validation_status: VALIDATED - independent implementations confirm pattern.

claims.claim: /compact with targeted hint prevents critical context loss vs bare /compact
claims.citation: Never run bare /compact. Always provide context hint: /compact focus on auth refactor, drop test debugging. This tells Claude what to preserve vs discard during compaction, preventing critical context loss.

claims.claim: MindBranches session fast rules (related follow-up vs new task vs wrong path vs context heavy vs failed branch) are widely shared reference
claims.citation: Related follow-up, same working set -> Continue / New task -> /clear / Wrong path, same task -> /rewind (Esc Esc) / Same task, context getting heavy -> /compact [with hint] / Need lessons from failed branch -> HANDOVER.md first

claims.claim: PreCompact hook captures full session transcript (user messages, file mods, task events, sub-agents, skills, MCP tool usage) to JSON/markdown backup
claims.citation: Hook fires RIGHT BEFORE compaction, capturing full session transcript to a JSON/markdown backup. Extracts: user messages, file modifications (write/edit tool calls), task events, sub-agent invocations, loaded skills, MCP tool usage, build/test commands.

claims.claim: PreCompact hook requires async:true to avoid slowing down compaction
claims.citation: Implementation key: { 'async': true } // Required - don't slow down compaction

claims.claim: Community consensus on 60-75% as safe autocompact trigger; native settings.json config NOT available (multiple open GitHub issues)
claims.citation: Community consensus on 60-75% as safe autocompact trigger. Native settings.json config NOT available (multiple open GitHub issues: #11819, #15719, #25679, #28728, #34126, #46695). Workaround: CLAUDE_AUTOCOMPACT_PCT_OVERRIDE env var (1-100).

claims.claim: claudefa.st recommends 80% threshold to stop complex multi-file work; buildtolaunch recommends 60% threshold
claims.citation: Power-user config pattern notes: 80% threshold: stop complex multi-file work (claudefa.st recommendation) / 60% threshold: community recommendation for proactive compaction

claims.claim: 33K tokens reserved by auto-compact buffer (non-negotiable); performance degradation at 20% context utilization
claims.citation: 33K tokens: reserved by auto-compact buffer (non-negotiable) / 20%: context where quality degradation begins (claudefa.st finding)

claims.claim: Session per task doctrine: new topic = new chat, no exceptions; effective session cost drops from $2.87 to $0.94 when switching to focused isolated sessions
claims.citation: Canonical rule: When you start a new task, start a new session. Effective session cost drops from $2.87 to $0.94 average when switching from long drag-on sessions to focused isolated sessions. Community shorthand: 'New topic = new chat. No exceptions.'

claims.claim: 2-hour sessions result in 2-3 compactions with compounding summary dilution; effective high-quality window ~400K of 1M advertised
claims.citation: 2-hour session = 2-3 compactions = compounding summary dilution / Performance degradation begins at 20% context utilization (not 80%) / Effective high-quality window: ~400K tokens of the advertised 1M (from 6852-session study)

claims.claim: Plan acceptance (native ~2026-02 feature) automatically clears context, giving plan execution fresh context window
claims.citation: Native Claude Code feature (shipped ~2026-02): accepting a plan automatically clears context, giving plan execution a fresh context window. Boris Cherny (creator): 'We found this helps keep Claude on track longer, and significantly improves plan adherence.'

claims.claim: claude-mem: 5 lifecycle hooks (SessionStart -> UserPromptSubmit -> PostToolUse -> Summary -> SessionEnd) with SQLite DB at ~/.claude-mem/claude-mem.db
claims.citation: Tool A: claude-mem (thedotmack/claude-mem) - 5 lifecycle hooks: SessionStart -> UserPromptSubmit -> PostToolUse -> Summary -> SessionEnd / SQLite3 DB at ~/.claude-mem/claude-mem.db / Worker on Express API port 37777

claims.claim: claude-memory-compiler: Karpathy LLM KB architecture with SessionEnd+PreCompact hooks; 6 PM auto-compilation; no RAG (structured index outperforms vector at 50-500 article scale)

claims.claim: Subagent isolation: use subagent when you need only conclusion, not tool output again; fresh 200K context window returns 1K-2K token summary to parent
claims.citation: Mental test: 'Will I need this tool output again, or just the conclusion?' If just the conclusion - use a subagent. Subagents get fresh 200K context windows; only 1K-2K token summaries return to parent session.

claims.claim: Subagent rule of thumb: anything requiring reading 3-4+ large files is solid subagent candidate
claims.citation: Rule of thumb: 'Anything requiring reading more than 3-4 large files is a solid subagent candidate.'

claims.claim: Hybrid manual context management: split monolithic CLAUDE.md into domain-specific files (policies.md, wot.md, queries.md); load only relevant files pre-session
claims.citation: Split monolithic CLAUDE.md into domain-specific files (e.g., policies.md, wot.md, queries.md). Session starts with manual summary of 'what matters today' before any file reads.

claims.claim: Opening context summary gets highest attention weight - earlier context more reliably referenced than context buried in middle
claims.citation: 'Earlier context is more reliably referenced than context buried in the middle.' - opening context summary gets highest attention weight

conflicts_flagged: CONFLICT 1: Compaction threshold recommendations diverge - buildtolaunch.substack recommends 60%, claudefa.st recommends 80%, Anthropic official gives no specific threshold. Resolution: likely workflow-dependent. 60% = aggressive (safe, costly), 80% = permissive (efficient, risky). Use 60-70% as default. [See R7.C8, R7.C9]

CONFLICT 2: 1M context window effectiveness - official Anthropic states 1M available, but empirical Scortier study (6852 sessions) shows effective quality window ~400K tokens; performance degradation at 20% utilization, not 80%. Treats practical budget ~300-400K. [See R7.C12]

CONFLICT 3: Adaptive thinking/effort level underpublicized - Scortier study shows 73% reasoning depth decline Jan->Mar 2026, but this workaround (CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL=max) is not widely advertised in official docs. [See R7.C27, R7.C28]
gaps_flagged: NAMING FRAGMENTATION: Three competing conventions for pre-compaction saves (HANDOVER.md vs SESSION-NOTES.md vs PROGRESS.md) with no canonical winner. Recommendation: SYNTHESIS should pick one standard. [R7.C24]

MISSING NATIVE CONFIG: autoCompactAt in settings.json (highly requested, 6 open GitHub issues as of 2026-04-17) remains unmerged. Users must resort to env var CLAUDE_AUTOCOMPACT_PCT_OVERRIDE workaround. Recommendation: SYNTHESIS note this as known gap. [R7.C25]
BENCHMARK GAP: No controlled comparison of manual PROGRESS.md vs automated claude-mem effectiveness. Tool adoption unvalidated. Recommendation: flag for future campaign or CRITIC validation. [R7.C26]

EFFORT LEVEL UNDERPUBLICIZED: 73% reasoning depth decline (Scortier study, Jan->Mar 2026) and CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL=max workaround are not widely broadcast in official Anthropic channels. High practical impact for power users. Recommendation: SYNTHESIS highlight this. [R7.C27]

X/TWITTER PAYWALL: Direct fetch blocked (402). Engagement metrics (790K views for bcherny hidden features thread) sourced from secondary sources, not authoritative X counts. Lower confidence on exact virality metrics. [R7.C30]
